# Independent audit of the sampled projective Ball-body obstruction

The complete note `candidate 3175dfaa311e9f49`
passes an independent mathematical audit.

- The two slope measures use the same continuous parametrization
  `x=y+kv` on both integer sides; therefore their ambient cap thresholds
  are respectively `u.v>=-a` and `u.v>=a`, as displayed. The separate
  central-fiber term retains the boundary mass for vertical caps.
- Convexity with the actual anchor proves the nested slice inclusions.
  The ray endpoints, extended gauges, integer endpoint inclusion, and
  fiber Jacobian `k^d` are all consistent, even for an anchor on the
  ambient boundary.
- The claimed convex hull has exactly the five positive-area fibers
  `D,Q,Q,Q,D`: every generator lies in Q, the middle slab is contained,
  and extremality of the two outer base coordinates fixes their fibers.
  The total mixed area is 16. Central inversion proves the stated
  one-half depth for every nonvertical central cut; the vertical
  central cuts have mass 10. Opposite nonvertical cuts at any candidate
  prove that no point has depth greater than one half.
- The positive projective density is exactly `1_Q+4 1_(D/2)`, with
  integral six. Direct radial integration gives the gauge
  `(1+s)/sqrt((1+s)^2+1)` on `(1,s)`, whose second derivative is
  strictly negative on the entire displayed interval.
- The exact midpoint inequality squares to `191/130>4/sqrt(10)` and
  then to `36481>27040`; all quantities squared are positive. The
  normalized endpoint construction converts failure of gauge
  convexity into actual failure of convexity of the radial body.

The obstruction concerns the sampled slope density. It does not
contradict the continuous external-contact theorem, which first proves
convexity of the relevant inverse power of its projected density. No
such convexity property holds or is invoked for this sampled density.

The supplied Fraction verifier `supporting computation verify_sampled_projective_ball_nonconvexity.py`
also passes. No correction is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
